A.text: A wire of natural length 2L, Young's modulus Y and cross-sectional area A is stretched and a mass m is suspended from the mid point of wire as shown in figure. The depression x produced in the wire is proportional to
A.sol_text:
Answer: (1)

Answer (2)
T = ((YA)/(2L)) × 2(√(L² + x²) - L)
= (YA)/L [L(1 + x²/L²)^(1/2) - L]
= (YA)/L × (x²/(2L))

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A monochromatic beam of light of wavelength 663 nm is incident normally on a surface produces a pressure of 10^(-6) N/m². The surface absorbs 75% of the incident light and reflects the rest. The number of photons incident per second on a unit area is
A.sol_text:
Answer : (1)
Hint:
Intensity = Energy/(Area − time)

Solution:
I = nhc/(λAt)
Pressure = I(1+n)/c = nhc(1+n)/(λAtc)
10^(-6) = (n × 6.63×10^(-34)(1+0.25))/(At × 663×10^(-9))
n/At = 10^21/1.25 = 8 × 10^20

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Diameter of a plano-convex lens is 6 cm and thickness at the centre is 3 mm. If the speed of light in the material of the lens is 2 × 10⁸ m/sec, the focal length of the lens is
A.sol_text:
Answer : (3)
Solution:

According to lens formula 1/f = (μ - 1)[1/R₁ - 1/R₂] The lens is plano-convex i.e., R₁ = R and R₂ = ∞ Hence 1/f = (μ-1)/R ⇒ f = R/(μ-1) Speed of light in medium of lens v = 2 × 10⁸ m/s
⇒ μ = c/v = (3×10⁸)/(2×10⁸) = 3/2 = 1.5 If r is the radius and y is the thickness of lens (at the centre), the radius of curvature R of its curved surface in accordance with the figure is given by
R² = r² + (R - y)² ⇒ r² + y² - 2Ry = 0 Neglecting y²;we get R = r²/(2y) = (6/2)²/(2×0.3) = 15 cm Hence
f = 15/(1.5-1) = 30 cm

A.text: A non-conducting piston of mass m and area S₀ divides a non-conducting, closed cylinder as shown in figure. Piston having mass m is connected with top wall of cylinder by a spring of spring constant k. Top part is evacuated and bottom part contains an ideal gas at pressure P₀ in equilibrium position. Adiabatic exponent is γ and in equilibrium length of each part is l. Ignoring friction the angular frequency for small oscillation of piston is

PV^γ = Constant

a = ((kdx + S₀γ₀dxdx)/(ml))
a = -((kl + γS₀P₀)/(ml)) dx
ω = √((kl + γP₀S₀)/(ml))

A.text: The potential energy of a particle of mass m executing SHM along x-axis is given by U = U₀ − U₀cosax(where U₀ is constant). The frequency of oscillation is
A.sol_text:

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Two rectangular blocks A and B of masses 2kg and 3kg respectively are connected by a spring of spring constant 10.8Nm⁻¹ and are placed on a frictionless horizontal surface. The block A was given an initial velocity of 0.15ms⁻¹ in the direction shown in the figure. The maximum compression of the spring during the motion is
A.sol_text:
As the block A moves with velocity 0.15ms⁻¹, it compresses the spring which pushes B towards right. A goes on compressing the spring till the velocity acquired by B becomes equal to the velocity of A, i.e, 0.15ms⁻¹. Let this velocity be v. Now, spring is in a state of maximum compression. Let x be the maximum compression at this stage.

0.15ms⁻¹ →

According to the law of conservation of linear momentum, we get m_A u = (m_A + m_B)v or v = (m_A u)/(m_A + m_B) = (2 × 0.15)/(2+3) = 0.06ms⁻¹

According to the law of conservation of energy ½m_A u² = ½(m_A + m_B)v² + ½kx²
½m_A u² - ½(m_A + m_B)v² = ½kx²
½ × 2 × (0.15)² - ½(2 + 3)(0.06)² = ½kx²
0.0225 - 0.009 = ½kx² or 0.0135 = ½kx² or x = √(0.027/k) = √(0.027/10.8) = 0.05m

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Uniform magnetic field B₀ exists in circular region, a ≤ r ≤ 2a. A charge particle (q, m) is projected from (a, 0) with velocity v₀î. Maximum value of v₀ so that particle does not exit the magnetic field region is

[Geometric diagram showing a right triangle with hypotenuse 2a, one leg a, and radius r marked]

(2a - r)² = r² + a²
4a² + r² - 4ar = r² + a²
3a² = 4ar, r = (3a/4)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Consider an ideal gas sample (of mass m) contained in a cylindrical vessel of volume V placed in the uniform gravitational field of the earth. If gas density at the bottom of the vessel is k times that at the top, density at the top of the vessel is equal to (temperature is same in the vessel)
A.sol_text:
dP = -ρg dh ⇒ dρ · (RT/M) = -ρg dh
⇒ log(ρ₂/ρ₁) = (Mgh)/(RT)
⇒ (RT/M) = (gh)/(log k)
(ρ₂ = density at bottom, ρ₁ = density of top)
Also, for vertical equilibrium of gas sample, (P₂ - P₁)A = mg
⇒ (ρ₂ - ρ₁)A(RT/M) = mgρ
⇒ ρ = (m log k)/(V(k-1)) [∵ ρ₁ = ρ₂/k = ρ]

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A parallel beam of light of all wavelengths greater than 3000 Å falls on a double slit in a Young's double slit experiment. It is observed that the wavelengths 3600 Å and 6000 Å are absent at a distance of 31.5 mm from the position of the central maximum, and the orders of the interference at this point for the two wavelengths differ by 7. If the distance between the slits and the screen is 1 m, the separation between the two slits is
A.sol_text:
Answer : (3)
Solution:
At x = 31.5 mm, both 3600 Å and 6000 Å produce minima. If the slit separation is d, then
xd/(Dλ₁) = n₁ + 1/2,  xd/(Dλ₂) = n₂ + 1/2

or, xd/D(1/λ₁ - 1/λ₂) = n₁ - n₂ = 7

Substituting the values, D = 1 m, λ₁ = 3600 Å, λ₂ = 6000 Å,
we get d = 0.2 mm

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A person measures the depth of a well by measuring the time interval between dropping a stone and receiving the sound of impact with the bottom of the well. The error in his measurement of time is δT = 0.01 seconds and he measures the depth of the well to be L = 20 meters. Take the acceleration due to gravity g = 10 ms⁻² and the velocity of sound is 300 ms⁻¹. Then the fractional error in the measurement, δL/L, is closest to
A.sol_text:
Answer : (1)
Solution:

[Diagram shows a well with depth L, stone falling time t₁, and sound travel time t₂]

t₁ = √(2L/g)

t₂ = L/v

∴ T = t₁ + t₂

⇒ T = √(2L/g) + L/v

⇒ ΔT = √(2/g) × (1/(2√L)) ΔL + (1/v) ΔL

⇒ 0.01 = (1/√5 × 1/(2×√20) + 1/300) ΔL

⇒ 0.01 = (1/20 + 1/300) ΔL

⇒ 0.01 = ((15+1)/300) ΔL

⇒ ΔL = (0.01 × 300)/16

∴ (ΔL/L) × 100 = 3/(16 × 20) × 100 = 1%

A.subject: Physics
A.text:
A certain atom emits light of wavelength 6000 Å and 5000 Å for the transition C to A and B to A respectively. Then
(i) Level C has a higher energy than level B
(ii) Level A has a lower energy than both levels B and C
(iii) The wavelength of light emitted for the transition from B to C is 1000 Å
(iv) The wavelength of light emitted for the transition from B to C is 30,000 Å
A.sol_text:
Answer : (2)
Solution:
E = 12400/λ
C to A → λ = 6000Å
B to A → λ = 5000Å
(E_C − E_A) < (E_B − E_A)
E_C < E_B
Now E_C − E_A = hC/6000 ... (i)
E_B − E_C = hC/5000 ... (ii)
on solving
E_B − E_C = hC/30000

So λ_{B→C} = 30000Å

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A proton collides with a stationary deuteron to form a ³He nucleus. For this reaction to take place, the proton must have a minimum kinetic energy K₀. If instead, a deuteron collides with a stationary proton to make a ³He nucleus, then it must have a minimum kinetic energy equal to
A.sol_text:
Answer: (1)
Solution:
Answer (A)
In case 1:
Colm: mv₀ = 3mv
⇒ v = v₀/3
COME: (1/2)mv₀² = (1/2)3m(v₀/3)² + U₀
⇒ U₀ = K₀ - K₀/3 = 2K₀/3
In case 2:
COLM: 2mv₀' = 3mv' ⇒ v' = (2/3)v₀'
COME: (1/2)2m(v₀')² = (1/2)3m(2/3 v₀')² + 2K₀/3
⇒ mv₀'² - (2/3)mv₀'² = 2K₀/3
⇒ (1/3)mv₀'² = 2K₀/3
⇒ (1/2)2mv₀'² = 2K₀

B.text: Radiations of wavelength 310 nm are incident on the emitter plate of photoelectric setup. Total power incident on the emitter is 100 watt. It is given that one electron is emitted for every 10^6 incident photons. The saturation current in the circuit is 25 × 10^(-k) A. Find the value of k.

Current = 25 μA

B.text: Two calorimeters A and B contain equal amount of water at temperatures 48°C and 80°C respectively. Mass of water in each of the calorimeters is 300 g. From calorimeter A, 100 g water is transferred into B and gently stirred until thermal equilibrium is established. A                          B
48°C                       80°C
300 g                      300 g

⇒ T₁ = 72°C

Then, 200 × (T₂ - 48) = 100 × (72 - T₂)

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text:
Consider the following reaction sequence

[Cyclohexane ring with COOH group (bold wedge) and CH₃ group (bold wedge)] →(SOCl₂) P →(NH₃) Q →(Br₂ + KOH) K

The product R among the following is
options: [Cyclohexane ring with NH₂ group (bold wedge) and CH₃ group (bold wedge)]
[Cyclohexane ring with NH₂ group (bold wedge) and CH₃ group (bold wedge)]
[Cyclohexane ring with NH₂ group (hatched wedge) and CH₃ group (hatched wedge)]
[Cyclohexane ring with CH₃ group (bold wedge) and CH₃ group (hatched wedge)]
A.sol_text:
Starting material: [Cyclohexane ring with COOH group (bold wedge) and CH₃ group (bold wedge)]

Step 1 - SOCl₂ treatment:
COOH → COCl (acid chloride formation)
Product P: [Cyclohexane ring with COCl group (bold wedge) and CH₃ group (bold wedge)]

Step 2 - NH₃ treatment:
COCl + NH₃ → CONH₂ (primary amide formation)
Product Q: [Cyclohexane ring with CONH₂ group (bold wedge) and CH₃ group (bold wedge)]

Step 3 - Br₂ + KOH treatment (Hofmann degradation):
CONH₂ is converted to NH₂ through Hofmann rearrangement
The carboxamide group is degraded, losing the carbonyl carbon
Product R: [Cyclohexane ring with NH₂ group (bold wedge) and CH₃ group (bold wedge)]

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If three distinct numbers a, b, c are in G.P. and the equations ax² + 2bx + c = 0 and dx² + 2ex + f = 0 have a common root, then which one of the following statements is correct?
options: d, e, f are in Arithmetic Progression
d, e, f are in Geometric Progression.
A.sol_text:
Since a, b, c are in G.P.
⇒ b² = ac

Given, ax² + 2bx + c = 0
⇒ ax² + 2√(ac)x + c = 0
⇒ (√(ax) + √c)² = 0
⇒ x = -√(c/a)

∴ ax² + 2bx + c = 0 and dx² + 2ex + f = 0 have common root
⇒ x = -√(c/a) must satisfy dx² + 2ex + f = 0

⇒ d · (c/a) + 2e(-√(c/a)) + f = 0
⇒ (dc/a) - (2e√c)/√a + f = 0
⇒ (d/a) - (2e/b) + (f/c) = 0
⇒ (2e/b) = (d/a) + (f/c)
⇒ (d/a), (e/b), (f/c) are in A.P.

A.text: Consider the differential equation, y²dx + (x - 1/y)dy = 0. If value of y is 1 when x = 1, then the value of x for which y = 2, is:

Its solution is

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The points P, Q, R, S on the sides OA, OB, OC and AB of a regular tetrahedron are coplanar. If OP/OA = 1/3, OQ/OB = 1/2, OR/OC = 1/3 and OS/AB = λ, then λ is equal to
options: No value of λ is possible
A.sol_text:
Let OA⃗ = a⃗, OB⃗ = b⃗ and OC⃗ = c⃗, then
AB⃗ = OB⃗ − OA⃗ = b⃗ − a⃗

and OP⃗ = (1/3)a⃗, OQ⃗ = (1/2)b⃗, OR⃗ = (1/3)c⃗
OS⃗ = λ(b⃗ − a⃗)
P, Q, R and S are coplanar, then
PS⃗ = αPQ⃗ + βPR⃗
OS⃗ − OP⃗ = α(OQ⃗ − OP⃗) + β(OR⃗ − OP⃗)
OS⃗ = αOQ⃗ + βOR⃗ + (1 − α − β)OP⃗
λ(b⃗ − a⃗) = α(b⃗)/2 + β(c⃗)/3 + (1 − α − β)(a⃗)/3
On comparing, −λ = (1−α−β)/3, λ = α/2
and β = 0
∴ −λ = (1−α)/3, λ = α/2
⇒ −3λ = 1 − 2λ
λ = −1

B.text: n balls are arranged to form an equilateral triangle such that first row consists of one ball, second row consists of two balls, third row consists of three balls and so on. 49 more balls are added to form a square. If each side of square contains 3 balls more than the ball contain by each side of the equilateral triangle, then the sum of digits n is
B.sol_text:
Answer : 06.00
Hint:
k(k+1)/2 + 49 = (k + 3)^2

Solution:
Let the number of rows in triangle is K.
1 + 2 + 3 + .... + K = n
n = K(K+1)/2

K(K+1)/2 + 49 = (K + 3)^2

K^2 + K + 98 = 2K^2 + 12K + 18
⇒ K = 5

Number of balls = n = K(K+1)/2 = 15

Sum of digits = 1 + 5 = 06
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let A = [a b c; b c a; c a b] is an orthogonal matrix and abc = -24 then the value of |a²b² + b²c² + c²a²| is equal to
B.sol_text:
Since A is an orthogonal matrix:
A^T · A = I

[a b c; b c a; c a b] · [a b c; b c a; c a b] = [1 0 0; 0 1 0; 0 0 1]

From this:
a² + b² + c² = 1 and ab + bc + ca = 0
∴ a + b + c = ±1

Now a²b² + b²c² + c²a² = (ab + bc + ca)² - 2abc(a + b + c)
= 0² - 2(-24)(±1)
= 0 - 2(-24)(±1)

∴ |a²b² + b²c² + c²a²| = 48
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

B.text: Let t = (1+z+z²)/(1-z+z²) is a real number for all values of z, then the value of |z| is (where z is a complex number, Im(z) ≠ 0)
B.sol_text:

Hence, z + 1/z ∈ ℝ

⇒ z + 1/z = z̄ + 1/z̄ ⇒ (z - z̄) = 1/z̄ - 1/z = (z-z̄)/(|z|²)

⇒ (z - z̄)(|z|² - 1) = 0

⇒ |z| = 1 (z = z̄ is not possible as z is not real)
